races.name: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Dubai Bling
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 4yo has won twice at 5f-6f on Good, goes well fresh (18 days), and Murphy's booking is significant; prominent style places him perfectly to exploit the anticipated lead battle without overexerting early, and his hg:p tongue-tie suggests the stable is optimising for maximum effort.

runners_data.name: Stratusnine
runners_data.note: Palmer runs his second string here alongside Dubai Bling, with Doyle aboard a horse who has placed in six of his last ten on Good going; the 6f form is strong but the step back to 5½f is a query, and he tends to sit handy rather than force the pace.

runners_data.name: West Acre
runners_data.note: George Scott has fired in three winners from twelve in the past fortnight, and Keenan takes the ride on a horse who ran well at 5f on Standaard but whose last two Good-ground runs at longer trips were poor; this trip looks sharper than ideal.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator whose three Good-ground wins at 6f are on the record, Hart partners a horse who will sit last or near-last and needs the leaders to truly exhaust each other; the 18-day freshener is a positive and he is unexposed at this shorter trip.

runners_data.name: Corolla Point
runners_data.note: Bethell's in-form yard (9/23 in 14 days) sends a horse who has won twice at 5f on Good and loves to sit just off the pace; Rodriguez has the ride on a horse who finished first and second in his last two 5f starts, making him a strong fit for the anticipated race shape.

runners_data.name: Lexington Blitz
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner who won at 5f on Good and has strong placed form at the trip; Cowell sends him here to make the pace, and the question is whether he can sustain his effort over the extra half-furlong when two rivals will be fighting him for the lead from the break.

runners_data.name: Candy
runners_data.note: Two distant efforts on Good ground at 5f recently and beaten 23 lengths last time out at the track; the one win came on Soft and the Good-going profile here is a concern, though the drop in weight may partially compensate.

runners_data.name: Against The Wind
runners_data.note: A front-runner returning from 97 days off, which is a significant fitness query despite Kevin Stott's booking; his Best Good-ground effort was a third and he has failed to win on this surface, so leading but not winning the pace battle seems his most likely role.

runners_data.name: Toca Madera
runners_data.note: Tudhope rides a horse with an unblemished all-Good-going record (15/15) and a win at 5f at this course; his hold-up style means he needs the leaders to come back to him, but his track and going affinity make him a live outsider if the pace is truly hot.

runners_data.name: Trefor
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good nine days ago and ran creditably at 5f previously; Hills and Shoemark team up on a horse whose recent form is patchy but whose last win was at the trip and going, and the quick turnaround is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: An 8yo who has placed in four of five on Good going including two seconds, but has no win on this surface; the hg:tv headgear combination suggests he needs maximum encouragement and Murphy's claim connection is low-key.

runners_data.name: Naana's Sparkle
runners_data.note: Has won twice on Good and twice placed, with a tidy profile at 5f; hg:t tongue-tie, prominent style, and a 22-day break are all benign factors — Lemos De Souza sends a consistent type who should sit handy and run her race.

runners_data.name: Spartan Arrow
runners_data.note: Seven recent finishes between 7th and 8th, with the form figure 077 telling a consistent story of missing; hg:b blinkers have not unlocked improvement on Good going and the pattern here offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Gold Star Hero
runners_data.note: Won three of his first four starts including two on Standaard, but his two Good-ground starts show a second and a patchy 5th-18th sequence; he is a confirmed front-runner who will compete for the early lead, and his freshness (11 days) is adequate.

runners_data.name: Toyotomi
runners_data.note: 60 days off and all of his six Good-going runs at 6f; the step down to 5½f combined with a lengthy break makes this a speculative angle, and his one win came on Soft — not an obvious profile for today.

runners_data.name: Apollo One
runners_data.note: An 8yo who has finished 3rd, 9th, 14th, 9th, and 10th in his last five on Good going; Colin Keane's booking is interesting for a horse rated 91 but the form is going the wrong way.

runners_data.name: Dapper Valley
runners_data.note: Two wins on Good going including one at 5f, and a strong recent run of 1-1-3 suggests genuine ability; a natural hold-up runner pushed into the midfield map because the rear of the field is overcrowded — Marquand is a sharp jockey who may manoeuvre better than most in this compressed pack, but 108 days off is a query.

runners_data.name: Air Force One
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Good and has three top-5 finishes on similar ground, so the going and trip suit; a true hold-up type who will struggle to get his natural position in this congested 22-runner sprint — McDonald knows the horse well and may seek to thread a path, but positional compromise is likely.

runners_data.name: Stormy Impact
runners_data.note: One of four redistributed hold-up types who will not get a clear run from the back in this shape; Fahey's yard is in form (5/31 in 14 days) but the horse's last six runs show only one top-5 finish at 5f on Good, and the positional squeeze makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: The Man
runners_data.note: Six consecutive finishes between 6th and 13th, with hg:tp headgear already in place suggesting previous concentration issues; a natural hold-up type squeezed into the midfield by traffic, and the recent form offers nothing to build on.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Triton
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Good four days ago — a very quick turnaround — and has hg:p headgear; a hold-up type mapped to midfield rather than the back, and while the recent form is live, the short recovery and positional compromise both work against landing this in a 22-runner sprint.

runners_data.name: Another Baar
runners_data.note: Four career wins on Good going but recent form reads 0-0-0-6-0-7; the hg:t tongue-tie is already fitted and the Irish raider Keatley sends him over with limited fanfare — a natural hold-up type who will be further back than ideal in a field this size.

races.paceDynamic: Lexington Blitz, Against The Wind, and Gold Star Hero are all confirmed front-runners in a 22-runner field over 5½f at York, making a fierce early gallop virtually certain — this is not a race where any of the three is likely to ease up and gift the others a soft lead. The pace triangle will stretch the field from the first furlong, compressing stamina reserves and putting a premium on horses who can travel efficiently behind the speed without burning matches. Prominent types tucked just off the battle — Dubai Bling, Corolla Point, Stratusnine, and Naana's Sparkle — are structurally best placed to capitalise as the front-runners trade blows and tie each other up in the closing stages. The race shape heavily favours hold-up horses in theory, but the field contains more genuine hold-up types than the sprint track can accommodate at the back: Dapper Valley, Air Force One, The Man, Stormy Impact, Ziggy's Triton, and Another Baar are all redistributed into the midfield map because the rear of the field will be too congested for all of them to operate at their natural pitch, meaning the horses most likely to actually secure the prominent positions behind the speed — Dubai Bling, Corolla Point, and Stratusnine — carry the clearest tactical advantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Burn, Prominents Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Lexington Blitz, Against The Wind, and Gold Star Hero fight it out up front and the leaders tie each other up entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The scorching early pace sets up a race where horses racing prominently but under restraint can exploit the momentum without the energy cost of setting it; Dubai Bling, Corolla Point, and Stratusnine are all proven at 5f-6f on Good ground and are ideally positioned to pounce on a collapsing front three.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Irons Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Lexington Blitz or Gold Star Hero — steals a decisive break while the other two neutralise each other.
scenarios.body: A divided pace effort between Against The Wind and one rival can paradoxically allow the quickest front-runner to slip the field on a flat, Good-ground surface where York's straight rewards honest galloping; Gold Star Hero's recent course-and-distance form and Lexington Blitz's 5f win record make them the primary candidates to steal a march.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Hold-Ups Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so violent that the field spreads wide and creates a clear late lane for horses coming from the rear.
scenarios.body: Dark Thirty and Trefor are the most credible genuine hold-up operators who may find the carnage up front sufficient to fuel a late finish; however, this scenario is tempered by the fact that several nominally hold-up types (Dapper Valley, Air Force One, The Man) are redistributed and will not truly be launching from the back, narrowing the pool of authentic closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Midfield Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves slightly less ferocious than expected and the field bunches in the final furlong with no clear winner emerging from any position.
scenarios.body: In a tight mass finish on Good ground, horses with the highest recent TS scores and cleanest form figures — Corolla Point and Naana's Sparkle — hold marginal advantages; this scenario is the least likely given the confirmed front-runner count but cannot be fully dismissed in a 22-runner handicap.

watchPoints.text: Lexington Blitz, Against The Wind, and Gold Star Hero are all confirmed front-runners — watch the first two furlongs closely to see which, if any, blinks first and concedes the lead, as the horse who gets the cleanest front at least cost is the most dangerous pacemaker in the race.

Corolla Point is the prominent-style runner whose profile fits this race shape most cleanly — watch him in the first half of the race: if Bethell's runner gets a clean passage just off the pace in stalls positions that suit, he becomes the primary danger to the front-runners.

Dapper Valley has been away 108 days and is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield because of congestion — watch how Tom Marquand deploys him from the gates; if he gets shuffled back to his natural position at the rear, his Style_Fit penalty applies and his chance diminishes sharply.

Toca Madera has run all 15 of his Good-going races on Good going and won at this course at 5f — watch his price move before the off, as Tudhope will know exactly what he needs and this horse is quietly well-qualified if the pace collapse materialises.

With 22 runners on a flat 5½f track, watch for draw bias effects in the early stages — horses drawn high may be squeezed into the rail and lose crucial early momentum in a race where the first two furlongs set every tactical decision that follows.

races.name: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Alfred Wallace
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer trained by Ed Walker who has won twice over 7f on good ground including this course, making him a strong profile fit for a pace-hot Acomb; Kieran Shoemark rides and 26 days since last run is no concern given consistent recent form.

runners_data.name: Big Cigar
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win at 6f on good ground for Richard & Fahey, but the step up to 7f is unproven and he faces a significant class jump into Group 3 company here; Oisin Orr takes the ride and his finishing speed at the trip is the key question.

runners_data.name: Clash Of Hearts
runners_data.note: Front-runner with a modest OR=83 who is out-classed on ratings in this Group 3 field; Adrian Keatley sends him over from Ireland but he is most likely to add to the early pace before fading in the straight.

runners_data.name: Confucius
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's prominent racer who has placed consistently at 6f on good ground, and the step to 7f suits a horse who has looked held up in finishes at shorter; Wayne Lordan takes the ride and three runs at Group level suggest he handles the class, though winning has eluded him.

runners_data.name: Fuel The Jet
runners_data.note: Top-rated front-runner at OR=120 who won over this exact 7f trip on good ground last time for Tom Clover; Neil Callan rides and while his pace-pressing style will be challenged by multiple rivals wanting the same real estate, he is the highest-quality horse in the lead group.

runners_data.name: Gentle Hurricane
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced Andrew Balding-trained prominent runner who is unbeaten in one start over 6f on good ground; Oisin Murphy rides and the step to 7f looks likely to suit a horse who was travelling powerfully when winning, though the lack of experience is the sole reservation.

runners_data.name: Haffner
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien combine on a front-runner who has placed twice at 7f on good ground and won over the same trip; the headgear flag is absent but his tendency to race prominently will see him embroiled in the early pace battle, and Moore may look to slot just off the leaders to preserve him.

runners_data.name: Siouxperb
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Archie Watson who won over 6f on good ground at last start, but his OR=89 is towards the lower end of this field and his trainer has had no winners in the past 14 days; the pace influence he provides may exceed his chance of lasting to the line over 7f in Group 3 company.

runners_data.name: Stardom Glory
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's prominent racer who is unbeaten at 6f on good ground in three career starts, with James Doyle booked; the 53-day absence is the notable flag, and whether he stays 7f is genuinely unknown, though his profile suggests he will be positioned to challenge if the trip proves within his compass.

runners_data.name: Trean
runners_data.note: Front-runner from P Twomey's yard who won last time over 7f on good ground at this course, wearing headgear, and is one of only two runners with a win over this exact track and trip; W J Lee rides and his bold-going style will put him in the mix for the lead immediately, though he faces fierce competition for that position.

runners_data.name: Vega King
runners_data.note: K R Burke's front-runner who stepped up to win over a mile last time on good ground, suggesting 7f is well within range; Clifford Lee rides and his OR=92 makes him a mid-table runner on ratings, but the stamina angle and versatility over trips could see him last longer than some of the pace rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Trean, Fuel The Jet, Haffner, Clash Of Hearts, Siouxperb, and Vega King all carry front-running profiles, meaning York's straight seven furlongs will be contested aggressively from the break, with multiple horses demanding the early lead and almost certainly setting a strong, unrelenting gallop. Trean brings headgear and a win over this exact course and distance, Fuel The Jet is the highest-rated front-runner at OR=120 and won his latest over 7f on good ground, and Ryan Moore aboard Haffner for Aidan O'Brien adds quality pressure at the front. With no single horse able to dictate comfortably and the pace likely to be fierce from the off, the race will be run at a genuinely searching tempo that strips out non-stayers and places a premium on class, stamina, and the ability to absorb a fast pace before finishing. This race shape heavily favours hold-up and prominent horses with proven 7f class who can stalk the battle from slightly off the pace and sustain their run through the final two furlongs — Alfred Wallace (H), Gentle Hurricane (P), and Confucius (P) are the profiles that stand to inherit the prize as the front-runners burn each other out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If the six front-running types set a genuine scorching gallop that fractures the field by halfway, leaving hold-up and prominent horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: The lead pack tears into each other over the first four furlongs and stops abruptly in the straight, handing the race to runners who have been able to conserve energy off the pace; Alfred Wallace and Gentle Hurricane, both comfortable at 7f on good ground with winning form, are ideally placed to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacer Gets Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Fuel The Jet or Trean manages to find a clear lead and control the fractions rather than being hustled into a messy speed duel.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes less brutal if one horse breaks cleanly and settles in front with minimal pressure from the others, meaning they can bowl along at a measured gallop and use their stamina reserves in the final two furlongs; Fuel The Jet's OR=120 and recent 7f win make him the likeliest beneficiary if this shape materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not catastrophic, and a horse sitting just behind the lead group can sustain a long run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Confucius and Gentle Hurricane, both tracking close to the pace from prominent positions, would benefit from a race run at a fast-but-manageable clip that rewards horses with both tactical speed and genuine 7f stamina; Gentle Hurricane's unbeaten profile and Confucius's consistent placed record at Group level make them strong candidates here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If several of the confirmed front-runners miss the break or are pulled back, leaving the race with a false or slow early tempo that rewards the horse on the lead.
scenarios.body: A muddling gallop would nullify the advantage of the hold-up horses and keep the front-runner's stamina reserves intact to kick clear inside the final furlong; Haffner, trained by Aidan O'Brien and handled by Ryan Moore, is the highest-quality horse likely to find himself in front if the pace unexpectedly settles.

watchPoints.text: Fuel The Jet and Trean will both be ridden to lead from the front — watch the opening two furlongs to see whether one dominates or whether they lock horns and drag the pace into damaging territory for the entire front group.

Gentle Hurricane is unbeaten but has only one career run at 6f — if the step to 7f exposes a stamina limitation under pressure in the final furlong, his market position will have flattered his true chance in this specific race shape.

Alfred Wallace won this course and trip last time out and profiles as the standout hold-up horse, but if the pace is somehow slow, his hold-up style leaves him vulnerable to being outmanoeuvred by horses with more tactical speed.

Ryan Moore may choose to drop Haffner just off the lead rather than commit fully to a front-running role — watch where he positions in the first furlong, as that choice will signal how Aidan O'Brien's camp reads the pace and whether Haffner is being ridden for a staying-on finish rather than an early lead.

Stardom Glory is 53 days since his last run and unproven at 7f — if James Doyle rides him prominently to get the trip, his finishing effort in the final furlong will reveal whether the yard has him ready and whether he genuinely stays the distance.

races.name: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Christmas Day
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in his last two starts including a win at 1m4f on good ground, Moore takes the ride for the powerful O'Brien yard; sits naturally prominent and this steady-pace scenario plays directly to his strengths — the 52-day break is the only minor query.

runners_data.name: Maltese Cross
runners_data.note: Haggas-trained with an excellent form record including three wins at 1m4f-plus; naturally a prominent racer but the depth of pace in this field means he is likely to find himself tracking further back than he'd like, which mildly tempers his chance in a shape that rewards early positioning.

runners_data.name: Antigua
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, tongue-tied, and OR 87 represents a significant class drop from the others — Whelan can dictate fully unchallenged, and if the pace is economical enough on good ground, a front-running steal cannot be dismissed despite the bare form reading against him.

runners_data.name: Galiyan
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's son of Galileo Gold won over 1m4f on good ground at Royal Ascot but, competing here against a wall of prominent types, is likely to find himself pressed further back than Murphy would choose — his STYLE_FIT of 0.93 flags the positional compromise as a genuine chance dampener.

runners_data.name: Pierre Bonnard
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan rides for O'Brien and the horse has solid place form at 1m2f-1m4f on good ground; a natural prominent type who should secure a forward pitch in a field where Antigua is the only leader, making him a straightforward tactical fit for the most likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Superior Choice
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins for Gosden including two at 1m2f on good ground give him the most progressive profile in the race; however, he is a natural prominent type who cannot get that position here and is mapped to midfield against his instincts — his STYLE_FIT of 0.92 should discount his chance until he proves he can win from off the pace.

races.paceDynamic: Antigua is the only confirmed front-runner in this six-horse Group 2, and with just one horse willing to lead, the early pace is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than pressured — Ronan Whelan can dictate terms at a measured gallop on good ground over 1m4f. Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard are the genuine prominent types who will sit just off the leader, while Maltese Cross, Galiyan, and Superior Choice are all natural prominent racers who cannot all occupy that ground and will be forced to track further back than ideal. This race shape — a single, uncontested front-runner setting a steady-to-fair tempo — strongly favours horses who can travel in the first three or four and produce a sustained galloping finish, suiting Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard, rather than horses relying on a late burst from an unfamiliar rearward position. The field holds more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate; Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard are best placed to actually secure their natural positions, while Galiyan and Superior Choice are most likely to find themselves racing off the pace against their instincts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Antigua controls a measured tempo and the race unfolds as a genuine staying test from 2f out, the horses tracking closest to the leader have the decisive positional advantage.
scenarios.body: Christmas Day, ideally placed just off the pace under Ryan Moore, can pounce once the tempo lifts in the straight, while Pierre Bonnard's proven stamina at 1m4f means he stays on relentlessly from his prominent berth.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Antigua is allowed to stride along unchallenged at a genuinely economical gallop and the tempo is never truly tested until very late.
scenarios.body: Ronan Whelan steals first run at the top of the straight and Antigua's rivals, having failed to close the gap early enough, cannot reel him in on good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Midfield Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners over-commit chasing Antigua and the tempo becomes genuinely demanding, creating a scenario where late-running horses benefit.
scenarios.body: Maltese Cross, though pushed back from his natural position, is a genuine Group-class performer whose form figures on good ground are strong enough to pounce if the race is truly run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Outsider Gains
scenarios.trigger: If fractious early running or a bunched finish scrambles positions and leaves the redistibuted prominent types — Galiyan and Superior Choice — able to secure their preferred ground after all.
scenarios.body: Superior Choice's unbeaten hat-trick of wins on good going gives him the profile to capitalise if pace and positioning fall his way, with Galiyan's class at 1m2f-1m4f also coming into play.

watchPoints.text: Watch Antigua's early fractions — if Whelan steals a large lead unchallenged, this becomes a very different race for the prominent brigade behind him, particularly Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard who must not let the gap grow.

Galiyan and Superior Choice cannot both race prominently; monitor the early stages to see which, if either, manages to push forward — whoever succeeds materially improves their chance versus the mapped scenario.

Christmas Day is 52 days since his last run and, while O'Brien horses return fit, watch his market move and paddock demeanour as any freshness could affect Ryan Moore's ability to settle him in the ideal position.

With only six runners on good ground over 1m4f, the race is likely to be slowly run early before quickening markedly in the straight — horses who travel smoothly in the first three will have a decisive advantage over those asked to close from out of position.

races.name: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almaqam
runners_data.note: Front-runner with strong record at this trip on good ground (9/13 in similar conditions), but faces a stiffer test than usual at the top level and is likely to be pressed early by Constitution River, which may blunt his effectiveness.|

runners_data.name: Devil's Advocate
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse wearing headgear, winless at this class level (0W/0P in similar going), and will need the pace to fully collapse ahead of him; Havlin will be patient but the raw form figures make this a tough ask.|

runners_data.name: Ombudsman
runners_data.note: Outstanding recent form — five wins from five — at this trip and on good ground, and Buick will slot him just off the lead where he consistently performs best; the standout profile in the field on current figures.|

runners_data.name: Pride Of Arras
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type by style, won at this trip and going most recently, though an OR of 114 pitches her at a significant class disadvantage against the principals; the staying profile is genuine and she could outrun her odds if the pace scenario suits.|

runners_data.name: Zaydann
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in five career starts and prominent by style, but all five wins came on soft/standard or heavy ground; stepping into Group 1 company on a firmer surface introduces a genuine unknown, and his natural position may be harder to secure in this congested field.|

runners_data.name: Action
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by nature, with his best efforts when able to sit close to the pace, but this congested field means he is unlikely to get that berth — his [STYLE_FIT=0.94] tag reflects the real cost of racing out of role here, and his modest recent form string (-42076) reinforces caution.|

runners_data.name: Constitution River
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in five starts, all on good ground, and Moore will have the tactical intelligence to either lead or settle just off Almaqam depending on the break; the class question at Group 1 level against older rivals is the only genuine doubt.|

runners_data.name: Hawk Mountain
runners_data.note: Placed in each of his last three including Group 1 level, wears headgear, and Wayne Lordan will aim to sit prominently but may find the pace too intense to get his spot; the step up from nine to ten furlongs has been handled but eleven furlongs could stretch him.|

runners_data.name: Item
runners_data.note: Three wins from five at ten furlongs on good ground, and Keane will look to sit in behind the pace; the Group 1 assignment is the biggest career test but the form profile (11-191) is solid, and this distance suits better than the soft-ground outing suggests.|

races.paceDynamic: Constitution River and Almaqam will contest the lead from the outset, creating a genuinely-run gallop over this 1m2½f on good ground at York — a track that stretches stamina and rewards horses that travel smoothly into position rather than those who expend energy fighting for the front. With Ombudsman, Zaydann, Hawk Mountain, and Item all wanting prominent positions, there is a material risk of congestion on the home turn two to three furlongs out, where York's configuration tends to compress the field. The field holds more front-running and prominent-type runners than the race shape can comfortably accommodate; Constitution River and Ombudsman are best-placed to actually secure the positions they want, given Moore's tactical authority and Buick's ability to slot in smoothly off a strong pace. This race shape — a contested, honest gallop with early positional friction — ultimately favours a high-class prominent or mid-prominent horse who can travel within the pace rather than chase it, making horses that settle handily just off the lead the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Constitution River and Almaqam set a true gallop and the race is run at a genuine, even tempo throughout
scenarios.body: Ombudsman settles in the slipstream off the strong pace, travels powerfully into contention, and his exceptional recent form (five wins from five at this trip and going) gives him the class edge when the field quickens two out; Constitution River, if he finds enough to sustain his effort from the front, has the unbeaten profile to hold on under Moore's judgement.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Constitution River breaks quickly, establishes full control unchallenged, and Almaqam settles for a secondary role without disputing
scenarios.body: Moore allows Constitution River to find a sustainable rhythm and the pace is controlled rather than truly pressured, suiting a horse with pure class and an unblemished five-from-five record at this track configuration; without genuine pressure from behind, the closers are denied the pace they need to get competitive and the race is won in the middle of the track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early battle between Constitution River and Almaqam is fierce enough to blunt both leaders and the pace is a true test
scenarios.body: Pride Of Arras or Devil's Advocate, genuine hold-up types sitting quietly in the rear, get a fast enough early sectional to launch a meaningful late run; Pride Of Arras won over this trip and going combination most recently and has the staying profile to benefit if the race burns itself out at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Scrambles Form
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion materialises two to three out, causing interference, checking, or positional loss for multiple fancied runners
scenarios.body: Action, though racing out of its natural role in the mapped midfield, could benefit if rivals find trouble and it gets a clear run; Zaydann's unbeaten record in conditions but absence of Group 1 experience at this level makes it a likely casualty of the chaos rather than a beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Constitution River and Almaqam are both confirmed front-runners — watch the first furlong for a genuine duel that could set a pace hot enough to compromise both leaders by the home turn.

Prominent congestion involving Ombudsman, Zaydann, Hawk Mountain, and Item makes the two-to-three-furlong-out bend at York a flashpoint — any checking or crowding here could compromise multiple market principals simultaneously.

Zaydann's entire win record has come on soft or standard-to-slow ground; watch how sharply he travels in the early stages on today's good surface as a real-time guide to whether the ground is an issue.

Action is racing well outside its natural prominent position — if it gets shuffled back further in the early scrimmage, watch whether Whelan can get competitive at all or simply makes up the numbers in the straight.

Pride Of Arras's sectional splits in the closing stages will reveal whether the honest pace has created a true staying test — if she's making ground in the final furlong, it signals the front-end battle was more intense than the market anticipated.

races.name: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Duke Of Oxford
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Michael Bell who arrives on a 19-day turnaround; his best Good-ground form is at 15f-20f and this 2m½f trip suits his stamina profile, though his recent form string (-15760) shows inconsistency and he has yet to place in similar-going form study (0W0P from 4).

runners_data.name: Prydwen
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for George Scott on a horse who won over 12f on Good last time and has strong staying credentials; 53 days off the track is worth noting, but the trainer is 3/12 over the past fortnight and Prydwen's Good-ground record (1W1P from 8) is solid if unspectacular for this level.

runners_data.name: Kirchner
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore is a significant booking for the four-year-old trained by James Owen, who arrives on the back of a 16f win on Good and a second at Sandown; styled naturally prominent, this trip (2m½f) is a career-furthest test, and whether his stamina holds over the distance is the key question.

runners_data.name: Small Fry
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners this Joseph O'Brien five-year-old who has placed twice in Good-ground staying races this season; runs prominently by nature and has the fitness edge on an 18-day return, though his 9/12f effort last time and a lengthy form line at 20f (6th) suggests this trip finds him at full stretch.

runners_data.name: Valedictory
runners_data.note: William Buick's presence on this John & Thady Gosden four-year-old is a major flag — Valedictory has won twice and placed twice in his last five on Good ground and has been progressive over 14f; a step up to 2m½f is uncharted territory but the trainer's 4/16 T14 record backs the confidence, and a hood (hg:b) is fitted.

runners_data.name: Mordor
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer partners this Gordon Elliott six-year-old who was third twice and won over 14f-24f in recent starts; 64 days off the track is the concern, and his best form has come at Galway and Heretfordshire rather than York-style flat, fast-ground tests — Good-going record shows 2W7P over 15 runs.

runners_data.name: Team Player
runners_data.note: Greg Fairley rides for Ewan Whillans on a lightly-weighted four-year-old who has won twice and placed twice from five career starts; equipped with tongue-tie and cheekpieces (hg:tp), has done his best work on Soft and Standard ground and the switch to Good at York at this level represents a notable step up.

runners_data.name: Manxman
runners_data.note: James Doyle partners this Simon & Ed Crisford six-year-old who has been absent 351 days — a fitness concern that cannot be ignored despite his 1W2P form at 16f on Good; fitted with a visor (hg:v) and returning to a course where he has run creditably, but the layoff at this class over 2m½f needs to be treated with caution.

runners_data.name: In The Breeze
runners_data.note: Henrietta Knight's eight-year-old won last time over 12f on Soft and was also successful over 12f on Good earlier in the season; the step up to 2m½f is a query and the form at this trip is limited, but Colin Keane's booking adds interest and the trainer's small but sharp operation (T14:1/2) suggests this is a live runner.

runners_data.name: Boatswain
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Standard and has placed twice in staying company; this Crisford four-year-old is naturally a prominent racer but with so many rivals seeking the same early ground, he is likely to find himself further back than ideal — his Good-ground record (0W2P from 6) doesn't inspire at this level.

runners_data.name: Westminster Moon
runners_data.note: Robbie Colgan's mount for A J Martin landed a 14f York win on Good last time out; a genuine hold-up performer whose record over longer trips has been patchy (13th twice over 17-20f), he needs everything to fall right and the 23-day turnaround keeps him fresh.

runners_data.name: Shrimp Shady
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's in-form four-year-old has three wins from his last six including a 16f and 18f victory on Good; by nature a prominent racer, he ran only 11 days ago and the quick return may temper his chance if this race tests his stamina reserve — the Good-ground form (3W4P) is his strongest qualification.

runners_data.name: Kilmeaden
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's four-year-old arrives 11 days after his last run with a visor fitted (hg:v) and a record of 1W3P over 12-17f on Good; he has genuine pace inclinations but is likely to be squeezed back in this congested field — his Good-ground record (1W3P from 7) at this OR (90) is respectable without being compelling.

runners_data.name: Ghaiyya
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, Rossa Ryan will enjoy a clear lead for Charlie Johnston's four-year-old; Good-ground record is by far the best pace data point in the field (12/15 runs, 4W6P), but this trip (2m½f) is a career-furthest test and the question is whether his front-running style can be sustained over the extra distance.

runners_data.name: Fireblade
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's five-year-old has placed consistently — thirds and seconds at 12-16f on Good — but has never won on Good ground in 13 attempts (2W8P) and that record on this surface dampens enthusiasm; naturally seeks a prominent pitch but is one of several horses who won't get that position here.

runners_data.name: Ride The Thunder
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old has placed six times from ten Good-ground starts (1W6P) and third in his most recent 16f race suggests solid staying form; inclined to race prominently but Varian's recent 6/22 T14 form and the redistribution away from his natural position may blunt his chance unless he travels exceptionally well.

runners_data.name: Mountain Road
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's seven-year-old has an excellent recent run of form — 3rd, 1st, 5th, 3rd, 3rd — and won over 16f on Good earlier this season; claiming rider Lauren Young (5) is relevant for the weight pull, and Mountain Road is another horse who wants to race prominently but will likely find that ground taken — Good-going record of 2W4P from 10 is workmanlike.

races.paceDynamic: Ghaiyya is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead, Rossa Ryan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m½f trip on Good ground — the conditions suit a horse who sets an honest but unbruising pace. Behind him, seven runners carry genuine prominent intentions into a space that can accommodate perhaps three or four: Small Fry, Kirchner, Valedictory, Mordor, Team Player, Manxman and In The Breeze will all be bidding for the same early positions, creating a scrambling, elbow-jostling contest for the seats 2-5 lengths off the leader through the long York straight approach. The redistribution of Boatswain, Shrimp Shady, Kilmeaden, Fireblade, Ride The Thunder and Mountain Road confirms this field holds far more prominent-minded horses than the race shape can absorb — of those, Shrimp Shady (OR 91, in excellent recent form, 3W from 13 starts) and Ride The Thunder (strong closer record at this trip) are most likely to muscle into genuine prominent positions if they travel well, while the rest will be shuffled back into midfield against their nature. This race shape — a lone pace-setter under no pressure, surrounded by a congested prominent group who will burn more energy than Ghaiyya — strongly favours hold-up horses who can travel wide of trouble and launch from off the pace in the final quarter-mile, and prominent types with exceptional tactical intelligence rather than those who have to fight for position early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ghaiyya Dictates, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Ghaiyya sets a controlled, uncontested pace and the prominent group burns energy scrapping for position, leaving hold-up horses to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Ghaiyya leads at a fair but economical clip, the prominent cluster concertinas behind him entering the straight, and the race opens up for horses arriving with a sustained run from off the pace; Duke Of Oxford, Prydwen or Westminster Moon, all genuine hold-up types, get a clean run and pick up the weakening prominent group.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Sit-Steal Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion behind Ghaiyya resolves early, one prominent type settles in the slipstream and strikes decisively turning for home without over-racing.
scenarios.body: A horse like Valedictory or Kirchner — both with strong Good-ground records and powerful jockey bookings in Buick and Moore — tracks the leader without cost, then kicks clear at the 2f pole before hold-up horses can close; the lack of true pace pressure means the race is not run to suit pure closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group's early battle for position creates a genuine pace injection in the middle mile, causing the leader and front-rank horses to empty inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses who were forced rearward by the congestion — Duke Of Oxford and Prydwen in particular, with Prydwen's strong Good-ground and staying form — find an accelerating pace sets up a fast-finishing scenario; this requires genuine early pressure which is only possible if several prominent runners refuse to settle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Two Clear, Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Ghaiyya's uncontested lead becomes a commanding one and a single prominent tracker such as Shrimp Shady or Mordor is able to join him early without a fight and both simply outstay the field.
scenarios.body: The pair effectively race their rivals into the ground over the extended trip, with Ghaiyya's course-form on Good ground and Shrimp Shady's remarkable recent winning sequence giving them the fitness edge; hold-up horses find the race has been run too far from them to peg back.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion warning: Small Fry, Kirchner, Valedictory, Mordor, Team Player, Manxman and In The Breeze will all be competing for the same 2-5 position behind Ghaiyya — expect bumping and checking between the 1m and 5f markers as the pace drops and the pack contracts.

Manxman returns from 351 days off the track for Crisford — monitor in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of rustiness or over-exuberance after a year off; if he blows up mid-race he becomes a traffic hazard for those around him.

Ghaiyya's stamina over this career-furthest 2m½f trip is unproven — if Rossa Ryan feels him weakening before the 2f pole, the whole race shape inverts and prominent horses who have been stalking may be caught flat-footed while hold-up types sweep through.

Shrimp Shady ran only 11 days ago and, as a horse who will be forced to race deeper in the field than his natural style demands, watch whether Rob Hornby elects to push forward aggressively from an early stage — if he does, it could inject genuine pace into

races.name: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Naana's Shadow
runners_data.note: Four wins from six starts at five furlongs on good ground under Oisin Murphy for Katie Scott, who operates at 1/14 over 14 days — form reading 131191 screams consistency and she is perfectly drawn to race prominently at a realistic position in this field.

runners_data.name: Poatan
runners_data.note: David Egan rides a hold-up horse whose three good-ground runs at five furlongs have all produced placings — the 67-day absence is notable but George Scott sends horses out fit and the pace shape here is ideal for his patient style.

runners_data.name: Revival Power
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner who has led in nine of nine good-ground starts but has been out of the frame in his last three, including a blow-out (26th) recently — Tim Easterby's stable is firing (5/84 over 14 days) but Revival Power's form has clearly gone backwards.

runners_data.name: Baker Blue
runners_data.note: Three-day turnaround is a concern for a horse whose best effort was a second-place, and his recent 22nd finish on good ground at this trip raises a red flag — Dylan Cunha's yard keeps decent strike rates but Baker Blue's consistency is poor.

runners_data.name: Schrodinger's Cat
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's three-year-old has placed 15 times from 15 good-ground starts, including two wins, which is a remarkable consistency record — he races prominently and his 5f/good combination is proven, making him a solid each-way player in the prominent pile.

runners_data.name: Manatee Mehmas
runners_data.note: Headgear applied (t) for the first time which is worth noting for David O'Meara's yard; has won once at five furlongs on good and placed three more times, suggesting the distance and surface are right, but recent form has weakened from a win.

runners_data.name: Black Star Boy
runners_data.note: 61-day absence after a below-par seasonal return (15th), though his earlier five-furlong win on good was clear form — Ed Walker has the ability to have horses ready fresh and Kieran Shoemark takes over, so a bounce-back run is possible from a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Miss Yechance
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's filly carries a 3lb claimer (Jack Nicholls) which eases the weight assignment — she has been placed in 5/10 good-ground starts at five and six furlongs and is an honest, consistent prominent racer who would be suited to a strongly-run race.

runners_data.name: Tricky Tel
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's runner has three wins and multiple places this season, and his last two runs both produced victories at five or six furlongs on good — Jason Hart is a shrewd jockey in big fields and Tricky Tel's natural prominent style needs early positioning to be effective.

runners_data.name: Zain Primus
runners_data.note: All three career starts have been on the AW at Southwell, so this is a major surface and going switch into a competitive heritage handicap — John Butler's yard has form and the horse is clearly rated well enough, but the turf and field-size are genuine unknowns.

runners_data.name: Stargazed
runners_data.note: Wears a visor (v) and has struggled for consistency, with just one place in eight good-ground runs — the 0/1 win record on good and the pattern of weakening suggest this pace shape is unlikely to bring out his best despite Burke's strong book.

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' horse won twice earlier in the season and ran just three days ago, which is a quick turnaround — hold-up style suits the pace of this race, and his two good-ground wins at five furlongs are directly relevant, though recent form is mixed.

runners_data.name: Old Is Gold
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's runner has genuine prominent racing tendencies — the field is simply too loaded with front-runners and prominent types to allow him to secure that position naturally, so Saffie Osborne will likely have to accept a deeper draw than ideal, tempering his chance here.

runners_data.name: Shes Got A Brother
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason's mount is one of four confirmed leaders in a field that cannot accommodate all of them — Shes Got A Brother has not won in six attempts on good ground and recent form shows a decline from a promising earlier mark.

runners_data.name: Underwriter
runners_data.note: Flagged for finishing tendencies that fade in the final furlong, which is a structural concern in a race likely to test stamina — Luke Morris takes over for Michael Keady but the recent record of 0/10 wins over 14 days for the yard and the finishing pattern make this a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' hold-up horse has an excellent recent record, placing 8/14 times on good ground with two wins at five furlongs — Cam Hardie rides and the strong-pace scenario is exactly what Mighty Magnus requires to deliver his best late effort.

runners_data.name: Dolos Dream
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa on a horse with two wins from six on similar going, including a five-furlong victory — Ivan Furtado sends him with a live chance and De Sousa is adept at positioning a front-running type for a clean lead in a big field.

runners_data.name: Boston Dan
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's second string; nine starts have produced no wins on good ground and the recent run sequence (9-0-0-0-4-7) is deeply uninspiring — hold-up style leaves him needing plenty to go right in a field of this quality.

runners_data.name: Call Margot
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's hold-up filly has form figures of 18-6-2-7-1, showing she can win but from an inconsistent base — Connor Planas is a low-profile booking and the 18th on her most recent good-ground start at five furlongs does not encourage confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Revival Power, Baker Blue, Shes Got A Brother, and Dolos Dream all want to lead in a 19-runner field over York's straight five furlongs, guaranteeing a fierce early gallop with no quarter given from the stalls. The pace-setters will burn each other off, creating a genuine stamina test on good ground where the race is likely to be run at maximum tempo throughout — there is no easy slot for any of them to control and settle. Eight of the 19 runners seek prominent ground, meaning the first two furlongs will be a wall of horses fighting for position, with significant traffic danger between the 2f and 3f marks as the field strings out. Old Is Gold is a natural prominent-racer who has been mapped to midfield because more true front-running and prominent types exist in this field than positions can accommodate — Revival Power, Naana's Shadow, and Schrodinger's Cat are best placed to actually secure that territory. In a race with this much pace, the tactical verdict is clear: hold-up horses and late-finishers who can switch off and come through beaten rivals in the final furlong are structurally favoured by the pace shape this field creates.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front four burn each other out inside the first two furlongs, creating a true end-to-end sprint that sets up the back half of the field.
scenarios.body: The pace collapse empties the leaders and prominent brigade, leaving those held up with cover to accelerate into the gap in the final furlong on a flat, fair track that rewards late momentum. Poatan, Mighty Magnus, and One And Gone all thrive when given a strong pace to aim at and have the form to close aggressively.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one of Revival Power, Baker Blue, or Dolos Dream gains a fractional edge at the break and dictates a sustainable lead despite the pace pressure.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners fighting for space, the horse that breaks cleanest and finds the rail could dictate from the front at a pace that, while fast, remains within their comfort zone — York's flat five favours those who settle into a rhythm. Dolos Dream (Silvestre De Sousa) and Revival Power have both won at this trip on good and have the engine to hold rivals at bay.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Flyer Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the early scramble sees the front-runners check each other and a prominent but not leading horse slips into a perfect stalking position two lengths off the pace.
scenarios.body: Naana's Shadow, Schrodinger's Cat, and Tricky Tel all have the tactical speed to track the pace without over-committing, and any one of them can time a run from a clean position to get first run in the final furlong. Naana's Shadow in particular carries strong recent five-furlong form on good ground and is suited by the pressure-race conditions created by this field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Favours Wildcards
scenarios.trigger: If the congested break produces significant traffic interference for fancied runners and a lightly-raced or fresh horse threads through at long odds.
scenarios.body: Zain Primus arrives from AW handicap form and is unraced on turf in this company, meaning he is a genuine unknown who could benefit if rivals are checked or impeded. Boston Dan and Call Margot are outsiders whose form gives little encouragement but who could sneak into contention if the race falls apart ahead of them.

watchPoints.text: Revival Power, Baker Blue, and Shes Got A Brother will clash aggressively for the lead from the off — watch for bumping and interference in the first furlong as four confirmed leaders fight for the rail in a 19-runner straight-five field.

The prominent group (eight of 19 runners) creates a high probability of traffic trouble between the 2f and 3f mark — horses drawn wide or slow away will find themselves checking or switching, directly impacting hold-up runners like Poatan and Mighty Magnus.

Zain Primus has never run on turf and steps massively up in company from AW Southwell routes — monitor his pre-race behaviour and early market moves as an unexpected drift or contraction could signal stable confidence or the reverse.

Underwriter is flagged for fading finishes and races over the minimum trip in a strongly-run race — if backed, note that the pace shape actively exposes this tendency and any market support should be treated with caution.

Old Is Gold's redistribution from prominent to midfield is worth tracking in running — if Saffie Osborne attempts to push forward regardless and succeeds in getting a prominent pitch, his style-fit and Balding form make him more dangerous than his mapping position suggests.

races.name: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ruler's Pride
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for K.R. Burke and James Doyle who has won on good ground at this trip; ran 1st, 7th, 1st in last three and the form reversal bears watching — his good-ground record is spotless (3/3) and he is well-placed from 21 days off, but a big field and 135lbs makes this a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Havana Sprite
runners_data.note: Three wins from last three starts for James Tate including two over today's trip on good ground; the 5/5 similar-going record is the standout stat in the field and Hector Crouch settles her prominently — 134lbs and a rise in OR from those wins is the one question mark.

runners_data.name: Crystal Queen
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Fahey who returns after 63 days off — the layoff is the chief flag, but she won over 5f on good ground and has finished 1st or 2nd in three of four career runs; Warren Fentiman's claim helps at the weights and this longer trip looks likely to suit her late style.

runners_data.name: God Given Talent
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Haggas and Marquand stepping up to 6f after winning that trip first time; last two runs at 6f on good ground were 1st then 6th and 19th, so the form is inconsistent — tongue-tie fitted and 131lbs, but Haggas in form (6/39 T14) adds credibility.

runners_data.name: Dubai Champion
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Ben Haslam ridden by Ryan Moore, finishing 2nd last time over 6f on good ground after a win over 5f soft; the Moore booking is significant in a field this large and Dubai Champion has shown enough versatility to handle today's conditions — 3/4 on similar going.

runners_data.name: Savage Mariner
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Hugo Palmer who carries the ⚠ fade flag, having weakened at the finish in two of his last three; the blinkers are noted but he has beaten only 11th and 19th in his last two York-style efforts — Colin Keane rides but the finishing-line record is a concern.

runners_data.name: Persian Spring
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Richard Hannon who won over 6f on good ground earlier this season but has since finished 10th and 18th; four runs on similar going (1W1P) suggests the form is there on paper but the recent trajectory is sharply downward.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Glory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Charles Hills with Kieran Shoemark; only 2/4 on similar going (both good-to-firm or firm wins) and the two Good-ground runs produced 4th and 11th — in a three-way pace battle he will likely burn himself out, but if the others falter he could steal it.

runners_data.name: Underdog
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up from 5f for Richard Spencer; won over 5f on good ground but has finished 10th, 5th, and 15th in subsequent starts — Saffie Osborne rides but the OR drop to 85 and recent form make this a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Jumeirah Storm
runners_data.note: Prominent type who ran 2nd, 1st, 4th in three starts over 6f on good ground — an excellent record at today's trip and going combination; the hood worn previously suits a horse who is keen, and Neil Callan's record at 0/13 in the trainer's last-14 is a negative angle.

runners_data.name: Peaceful Warrior
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Kevin Ryan with just two runs — won over 6f on good and finished 4th in a stronger contest; 40 days off and only two runs in the book means there is still a large question mark, but Jamie Spencer's positional awareness in big-field handicaps is an asset.

runners_data.name: Elevating
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Richard Hannon returning just 5 days after his last run, which is an unusually quick turnaround; won over 5f on good ground and finished 2nd over 6f — the 4/4 similar-going record encourages, though Hannon's stable is a busy operation and the quick return needs explaining.

runners_data.name: Towelontheterrace
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Jennie Candlish who won over 6f on good ground; 2/3 on similar going and only 4 winners from 10 in trainer's last 14 day strike rate — in a three-way lead battle this horse is likely to be found out over the final furlong even if it helps set the fractions.

runners_data.name: The Dancing Pirate
runners_data.note: Unquantified style horse for Andrew Balding ridden by Oisin Murphy, with form of 4-4-2-7 showing one placed effort; 4/4 on similar going but the best finish was 2nd and Murphy will need to navigate a 22-runner field from an awkward positional spot — the hood (hg:p) flags keenness.

runners_data.name: Rlasthope
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 6f on standard ground but has a patchy record on today's good going (1/5 similar going); 3rd twice and 2nd once in recent starts suggests consistency without the required finishing kick, and the soft/standard form is better than today's surface profile.

runners_data.name: Henley On Thames
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner for Kevin Philippart De Foy, who won over 6f on good ground last time; the 4/4 similar-going record is strong (1W3P) but racing three-wide in a pace scrum with Sovereign Glory and Towelontheterrace is likely to cost him dearly unless those rivals fold — David Egan rides.

runners_data.name: Super Tuscan
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Eve Johnson Houghton who won over 6f on good ground; Oliver Carmichael's 7lb claim eases the weight burden but the 19-day turnaround and inconsistent finishing positions (6-5-1-4-5) make this a hit-or-miss profile in a large, fast-run field.

runners_data.name: Note To Self
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Gosden trained by John & Thady; placed twice in four starts (3rd and 2nd) with the better form over 6-7f on good ground — Shane Foley rides and the staying-on profile suits if the pace genuinely collapses in the final furlong, but the 22-runner field is a real navigation test.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Adrian Keatley who finished 3rd over 5f on good ground last time; the hood (hg:p) is a headgear flag, Silvestre De Sousa rides, but a 14th on standard ground suggests the good-going record (2/3) may flatter — De Sousa's positional skill will be needed to get a clear run.

runners_data.name: Bear Lee
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Easterby who won over 5f on good ground; three runs only, finishing 4-1-4, and Joanna Mason's claim helps — the step up to 6f is unexplored and from this wide field position a late run requires a gap that is far from guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Sue's Last Chance
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up filly for Fahey who has finished 5th, 6th, and 8th in three starts, all over 6f on good ground — her true style is rear of field but the sheer volume of hold-up types in this race means she will be racing in a congested section with no easy passage; the OR 75 and 0W0P career record make improvement a necessity.

runners_data.name: Brandenburg
runners_data.note: Ann Duffield's runner is a natural prominent racer with two wins including over 6f on good ground, but the field's pace congestion means he is unlikely to secure his preferred handy berth — Luke Morris will have to adapt, and racing out of role from a position he could not get to undermines what is otherwise a solid form profile (1W2P on similar going).

races.paceDynamic: Sovereign Glory, Towelontheterrace, and Henley On Thames are all confirmed front-runners in a 22-runner field, guaranteeing a strong gallop from the outset over York's straight 6f on good ground — this is not a race that will be allowed to develop slowly. Nine runners want to race prominently, creating a wall of horses hunting the first two furlongs, with serious traffic and interference risk 2-3 furlongs out as the field fans and jostles for position. The redistribution pressure is real: Brandenburg is a natural prominent type and Sue's Last Chance a genuine hold-up horse, but both are unlikely to secure their preferred slots in this congested shape — Brandenburg will be shuffled wider than ideal and Sue's Last Chance will struggle to find the clean late passage a true closer needs in such a big, fast field. This race shape strongly favours horses who can settle just off the pace in the first three or four, avoid the mid-race scrum, and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — the true prominent-to-midfield profile racing from a clean position, not the horses forced to the rear against their will.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners set a genuinely strong gallop and the prominent horses just off them travel smoothly into the straight with cover.
scenarios.body: The breakneck early pace burns off the pace-setters and the winners emerge from the chasing pack two wide with momentum; horses who can race handily without getting trapped in traffic will dominate the final furlong on good ground at York.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Ups Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go so hard that they blow up dramatically, opening a late gap for genuine closers to swoop.
scenarios.body: An unsustainably fierce early tempo creates a vacuum in the final furlong and horses coming from mid-to-rear who have been undisturbed in traffic find a clean run; York's straight track rewards a late surge when pace genuinely collapses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Pacer Gets Clear, Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners, most likely Sovereign Glory or Towelontheterrace, gets a soft lead with the other two checked back early.
scenarios.body: A single horse dictates from the front at a controlled but honest gallop, sets its own fractions, and proves hard to peg back; prominent horses without cover will be exposed and the leader who gets a clear passage banks the fractions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Wide Finisher
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes severe interference 2-3 furlongs out and several fancied runners are checked or blocked.
scenarios.body: A wide-travelling horse who has avoided the entire mid-race chaos arrives late and fresh while the main protagonists check each other; this is a low-probability shape but a large field on a straight track does produce it occasionally.

watchPoints.text: Sovereign Glory, Towelontheterrace, and Henley On Thames — three confirmed front-runners will inevitably clash for position in the first furlong, risking interference or a pace implosion that distorts the entire race shape.

The nine prominent-position horses create severe congestion between 2-3 furlongs out where York's straight narrows the margins — horses drawn wide may be forced even wider, while those inside risk being boxed in behind a wall of rivals.

Brandenburg — a natural prominent type redistributed to midfield who is racing out of role; if Luke Morris cannot recover a handy position early, Brandenburg's winning form becomes largely irrelevant to how this race unfolds.
Crystal Queen — 63 days off the track for Fahey is the longest layoff in the field and while the stable is in decent form, the hold-up filly will need to reacclimatise quickly in a 22-runner sprint.
